co_morrison_evergreen_littleton.blurb: This Front Range cluster stretches from the foothills town of Morrison up toward Evergreen, and it is mainly a bouldering destination. Boulder problems make up the large majority, with a wide spread from easy warm-ups through the V5 to V8 range and a handful of very hard lines. Roped climbing is a small side offering: trad and sport routes, mostly in the 5.9 to 5.12 range, scattered across small crags. The biggest sub-area is Alderfer/Three Sisters Park, where the boulders are granite; its east side sits in shaded pine forest while the west side is an open, sunnier field with broad views. Morrison Boulders, Juniper Pass and Bell Park add more variety within a short drive of each other.

or_southwest_oregon.blurb: Southwest Oregon spans the area around Roseburg and the Umpqua National Forest down to the Rogue Valley near Medford and Ashland. Sport climbing dominates, with most routes falling between about 5.8 and 5.11 and a solid core of 5.10s; trad, top-rope and bouldering fill out the rest, along with a few aid and alpine lines. The largest concentrations are at the Callahans, Terra Nova and Rattlesnake. Rattlesnake is a single-pitch sport crag on welded tuff, where rock quality ranges from solid to loose, buttresses run roughly 40 to 100 feet, and spring and fall are the best times (summer gets hot). Multi-pitch adventure climbing can be found at McKinley Rock, Acker Rock and Rabbit Ears.

sd_mount_rushmore_national_memorial.blurb: Part of the Needles country of the southern Black Hills, this area offers climbing on pegmatite granite, from boulder problems to trad routes of several hundred feet. Bouldering is the biggest share, followed by sport and then trad. Sport and trad routes run mostly from 5.7 to 5.11 with a hard tail up to the low 5.12s and 5.13s, and boulder problems cluster between V1 and V8. Rock quality is generally very good. Cliffs face every direction, so the season stretches from spring through fall, with the odd winter day. Mount Baldy is the main bouldering zone, while South Seas, Breezy Point, Chopping Block, Magna Carta and Emancipation hold the roped climbing. Many of the crystalline-granite routes are well bolted and suit moderate climbers.

ca_redwood_coast.blurb: The Redwood Coast covers the far northwest corner of California, from Arcata and Eureka up the shoreline and inland along Highway 299 toward the Trinity country. It is quiet and remote, and the climbing is mostly sport, with a notable share of bouldering, some trad and a few top-ropes. Routes sit largely in the 5.9 to 5.12 range, with boulder problems mostly V0 to V6. The rock varies by area: limestone at Trinity Arêtes, Marble Caves and Cecilville Bluffs, sandstone at Promontory, quartzite at Land Of The Lost, and granite in the Trinity Alps. Limestone climbs year-round in some form; Trinity Arêtes is mainly a summer crag, while Marble Caves and Cecilville Bluffs shine from fall through spring. Beach boulders line the coast.

co_buena_vista.blurb: Buena Vista sits on the east side of the Arkansas River Valley, beneath the Collegiate Peaks. Crags are granite, from about 40 to 500 feet tall, set in low, semi-arid mountains. Bouldering accounts for about half of the climbs and runs year-round, with most problems between V1 and V6 and a few much harder. Trad is the next biggest style, then sport, mostly 5.8 to 5.11 with a few 5.12s. Bob's Rock, Transmitter Tower and the Turtle Rocks are popular roped destinations, and Arkansas Valley Bouldering is the largest bouldering zone. Summer afternoons bring thunderstorms off the high peaks; the climate is dry enough that the valley can be climbed in nearly any season.

nc_2_northern_mountains_region.blurb: This part of western North Carolina lies northeast of Asheville, with most climbing between Boone and Morganton. Trad is the main event, followed by bouldering, with some sport routes, top-ropes and a little ice. Trad and sport grades are mostly 5.9 to 5.12, with a good number of moderates, and boulder problems run from easy to V8 and beyond. Linville Gorge is by far the biggest area and the heart of the region: the rock is quartzite, typically low angle, with routes that can wander and some route-finding. It offers easy multipitch climbs through to hard ones, and a good setting for learning to lead multipitch. Ship Rock, The Dump and Lees-McRae College add more variety, and several boulder fields lie scattered nearby.
